topic: Pablo Escobar Brought Four Hippos to His Ranch and Now Colombia Cannot Stop Them
research_summary: Four hippos (three females, one male) were imported in 1981 from a U.S. zoo for Pablo Escobar's private menagerie at Hacienda Nápoles in the middle Magdalena River basin. After Escobar's 1993 death, most animals were dispersed to zoos but the hippos were left because they were difficult to transport; they bred and spread. Peer-reviewed work (Subalusky et al. 2019 Oryx/NSF preprint; Shurin et al. 2020 Ecology; a 2023 Scientific Reports modelling paper led by Subalusky) documents rapid growth (~7-14.5%/yr, ~9.6%/yr in one model), projections exceeding 1,000 by 2050, ecosystem engineering effects (terrestrial nutrient import, cyanobacteria dominance, altered dissolved-oxygen/eutrophication), and the narrow management window. Government and news sources document the 2022 invasive-species declaration and 2023 sterilisation/cull plan. Guinness recognised the population as the largest invasive species. Comparable cases carried by independent primary sources: Burmese pythons in the Florida Everglades (USGS/PNAS Dorcas et al. 2012, ~99% mammal declines) and cane toads in Australia (introduced 1935, spread over 1.5 million km2, IUCN worst-100). Strongest openly readable sources: Nature/Scientific Reports, NSF PAR repository PDF, subaluskylab.com PDF, USGS government pages, Smithsonian Magazine, PubMed/PMC, biorxiv, open-access MDPI/Nature. Attrition budgeted: some ResearchGate, ScienceDirect, pressreader and portal pages likely gated and were used sparingly or flagged.

claims.claim: Four hippos — three females and one male — were imported to Colombia in 1981 from a zoo in the United States for Pablo Escobar's private zoo at Hacienda Nápoles.

claims.claim: The original four hippos were part of Escobar's effort to build an open-door zoo at Hacienda Nápoles, his large farm in the Magdalena River basin.
claims.support_quote: Drug trafficker Pablo Escobar brought them as part of his project to build an open-door zoo at Hacienda Napoles, his large farm in the Magdalena River Basin.

claims.claim: The imported hippos stocked a private menagerie at Hacienda Nápoles that also included giraffes, zebras and concrete dinosaurs.

claims.claim: After Escobar's death in 1993 the zoo was closed, but the hippos were left on site because they were difficult to transport, and they began to reproduce and disperse into the surrounding landscape.
claims.support_quote: After Escobar's death in 1993, the zoo was closed, but the hippos were left on site due to challenges with transporting them to new habitats, and they began to reproduce and disperse into the surrounding landscape.

claims.claim: After Escobar's 1993 death most animals at the abandoned estate died from lack of care or were transferred to zoos, and only the hippos and their offspring remained.
claims.support_quote: Most animals died due to lack of care; others were transferred to zoos.

claims.claim: Anecdotal hippo observations have been reported nearly 400 km from the original release site along the Magdalena River, near Magangué.
